detailed_rationale:
Eureka Forbes has been evolving from a water-purifier-centric business into a multi-category 'health and hygiene' company - water purifiers, water softeners, vacuum cleaners (increasingly robotics-led, now 65-66% of vacuum-cleaner category revenue), and air purifiers (which grew 2.7x in FY26). FY26 marked the second consecutive year of double-digit revenue growth (+11.3% to Rs 2,710cr), with adjusted EBITDA up 16.4% to Rs 332cr at a 12.2% margin (+55bps YoY) - Q4 alone hit the company's highest-ever adjusted EBITDA margin of 13.2% on revenue of Rs 684cr (+11.6% YoY). This is a genuine, multi-year, diversified growth story rather than a single-category or one-off pop, and the newer categories (robotics, air purifiers, water softeners) are growing fast enough to be a real second growth engine alongside the legacy water-purifier base (we found no credible evidence, despite an initial conflicting search snippet, that the company has divested its core water-purifier business - a follow-up source explicitly confirms water purifiers remain a growing category for the company today).

The gap between this operating story and the quant scorecard is capital efficiency: ROE of just 2.5% and ROCE of 5.2% translate into a quality_score of only 9.8/100, among the lowest in this batch, despite the healthy revenue and EBITDA trends. This suggests either a heavy asset/goodwill base, working-capital intensity typical of a large direct-sales/service-network model, or costs below the EBITDA line (depreciation, interest, tax) that are absorbing most of the operating improvement before it reaches shareholders - we did not find FY26 PAT figures to confirm whether net-profit conversion has started to catch up with the EBITDA trend. Balance sheet leverage itself is a non-issue (D/E ~0.006, interest coverage ~39x), so this is a returns-on-capital-efficiency question, not a solvency one.
recommendation_rationale: The top-line and EBITDA-margin story is genuinely encouraging and diversified across multiple product categories, but the persistently weak ROE/ROCE - unrelated to any leverage or solvency issue - means growth has not yet been converting into shareholder returns at a rate that would justify a ~56x trailing multiple. Without confirmed evidence that bottom-line profitability is closing the gap with the operating-level improvement, we do not see enough to rescue this to Hold.
summary: Eureka Forbes has built real momentum across water purifiers, robotics-led vacuum cleaners, air purifiers and water softeners, with two straight years of double-digit revenue growth and improving margins. However, returns on capital remain weak, meaning that growth has not yet clearly translated into shareholder value at a pace that supports the current valuation, and we recommend Sell.
positive_para: Eureka Forbes has diversified successfully beyond its original water-purifier base - air purifiers grew 2.7x in FY26 and robotics now drives roughly two-thirds of vacuum-cleaner category revenue - while maintaining double-digit overall revenue growth for a second straight year and hitting a record quarterly EBITDA margin (13.2%). The balance sheet carries essentially no debt, removing solvency risk from the picture entirely.
negative_para: Despite the healthy top-line and EBITDA trends, ROE (2.5%) and ROCE (5.2%) remain very weak, and we could not confirm from available FY26 disclosures whether net profit is converging toward the EBITDA improvement or continuing to lag it. A near-zero-debt balance sheet is a genuine strength, but it also means the weak returns cannot be blamed on leverage - the underlying capital efficiency of the business model itself needs to improve for the growth story to translate into shareholder value at the current valuation.
reverse_dcf_judgment: A ~55.7x trailing multiple assumes the growth and margin-improvement trend not only continues but also finally converts into materially better returns on capital - plausible given the diversification into higher-growth categories, but not yet evidenced in the ROE/ROCE data available to us. Judgment: rich until bottom-line conversion is demonstrated.
